articles.title: Monta un equipazo 'de Gala' y multiplica tus puntos
articles.standfirst: Arranca la nueva Liga Top Capitán con créditos y dos invitaciones para la gran fiesta del deporte
articles.summary: Arranca la nueva Liga Top Capitán con créditos y dos invitaciones para la gran fiesta del deporte
articles.body: A una semana solo del pistoletazo de salida a la temporada 26-27 rematamos el menú competitivo del Movistar Fantasy MARCA con la liga oficial Top Capitán (a final de mes lanzaremos la Champions). En este concurso podréis utilizar la nueva funcionalidad que multiplica los puntos del jugador al que pongáis el brazalete (es gratis) y premia con mil créditos al mejor de cada jornada, además de invitación doble para la exclusiva Gala del Deporte de MARCA. Empezamos sin jugadores, con 200 millones para fichar, un ciclo de mercado diario (20 futbolistas), disponemos de tres cambios durante la jornada y sistema de puntuación 'Cronistas MARCA + Estadísticas'. En la descripción de la liga tenéis los criteros a seguir en caso de empate final. Todavía quedan días para el Alavés-Getafe (sábado, 15 a las 19:30 h.) y de mercado abierto (hasta el 1 de septiembre), pero no hay tiempo que perder y vamos perfilando una alineación para la nueva Liga Top Capitán. Nos ajustamos al presupuesto de 200 kilos y buscamos un chollazo que nos multiplique sus puntos x3. ¡Descarga aquí el Movistar Fantasy MARCA con más novedades que nunca! ¡Con nuevas competiciones como la Champions, el Mundial o la Premier! ¡Con más premios! ¡Y con más opciones de personalización! Síguenos en X @FantasyMARCA. También tienes contenido diario en MARCA.com y semanal en el periódico, en el canal de MARCA en YouTube, en Radio MARCA y en TikTok.

articles.title: ‘Couldn't stay silent’: Iranian footballers reveal why they refused to sing anthem before seeking asylum in Australia
articles.summary: Football News: Iranian footballers Atefeh Ramezanisadeh and Fatemeh Pasandideh have broken their silence over the protest that preceded their decision to seek asylum.
articles.body: Iranian footballers Atefeh Ramezanisadeh and Fatemeh Pasandideh have broken their silence over the protest that preceded their decision to seek asylum in Australia, confirming that their refusal to sing Iran's national anthem at the Women's Asian Cup was a deliberate act of defiance against Tehran.The two players, who abandoned the Iranian delegation after the tournament and remained in Australia, spoke publicly for the first time since claiming asylum. Their interview with Australia's 60 Minutes was broadcast on Sunday, shedding new light on a gesture that had sparked intense debate over whether the players were mourning their country amid the escalating conflict or protesting against Iran's government.For Ramezanisadeh, 34, and Pasandideh, 22, the message was clear: they were standing with protesters back home.‘We just wanted to stand with our people’Iran's women's team had remained silent when the national anthem was played before their opening match against South Korea on March 2. The refusal immediately drew criticism in Iran, with sections of the country's media branding the players as traitors.At the time, however, the team did not publicly explain the decision.The gesture came shortly after US and Israeli attacks on Iran began on February 28, leading some observers to interpret the silence as an act of mourning. Others saw it as an act of resistance against Tehran.Ramezanisadeh has now confirmed that the latter was the reason for her silence."We just wanted to stand with our people. I was scared at times, but I just tried to do what was right and say that no one should be killed just for protesting," Ramezanisadeh told Nine Network through an interpreter.She acknowledged the enormous personal risk involved in refusing to sing the anthem.Ramezanisadeh said her silence "could have meant any form of torture" for her."But at that moment, the only thing that gave me peace and a clear conscience was not singing it. I wanted to sing the anthem with pride and from my heart. But because of the situation in Iran, I really couldn't do it," she said.Pasandideh was equally direct about what motivated her."My people put their lives on the line and they were killed. Doing that was the absolute least we could do for them," Pasandideh said through an interpreter.Silence becomes a turning pointThe players' decision became even more significant after demonstrators in Australia called for the Iranian squad to be allowed to remain in the country rather than return home.The team eventually left Sydney on March 10, but the issue had already reached the highest levels of Australian politics.Australian Immigration Minister Tony Burke said the players had not been promised asylum when they made their decision."At that point, they had absolutely no information from us about the possibility of being able to stay," Burke said."The silence of itself was deeply significant," he added. "The reaction was the volcanic moment."The situation escalated further after then-US President Donald Trump publicly called for the Iranian players to be granted asylum and spoke to Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese about the issue.Albanese subsequently told Trump that four players and a team manager had accepted offers of humanitarian visas.Seven members of the Iranian delegation eventually accepted Australia's offer of asylum, but all except Ramezanisadeh and Pasandideh later changed their minds.The two women, meanwhile, decided to remain.‘I couldn't stay silent’Ramezanisadeh said the decision to stay in Australia came despite pressure from her parents, who urged her to return to Iran after receiving instructions from Iranian authorities."They tried to reassure me, saying: Nothing will happen to you. This is your home. You must return home.' But I told them my mind was made up and I was not coming back," she said.The decision has come at an enormous personal cost."Thinking that I might never be able to see my family again was heartbreaking, but I couldn't allow myself to be indifferent while so many young people were being killed by this regime. I couldn't stay silent, even though I miss my family so much," she added.Both players said they had not been in contact with their families in recent months, although they understood that their relatives had not been punished.Their decision to remain in Australia has also led to a new chapter in their football careers. Ramezanisadeh and Pasandideh now play for semi-professional club Wynnum Wolves in Brisbane and became Australian citizens in August.‘I don't want to put their lives in danger’Pasandideh said she had deliberately avoided asking her former teammates whether they wanted to return to Iran or whether they felt compelled to do so."We decided not to talk because I don't want to put their lives in danger," she said.Despite everything that has happened, her attachment to Iran remains strong."One of my biggest dreams is to be able to go back to Iran, but in different circumstances when the situation in Iran has changed and the people of Iran are happy and thriving. Then I will go back and see my family," she added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Champion’: Lionel Messi’s son Mateo captains Inter Miami Academy to Naples Cup title
articles.summary: Football News: Lionel Messi's son Mateo has taken another step in his budding football career, captaining the Inter Miami Academy to the Naples Cup title and giving .
articles.body: Lionel Messi's son Mateo has taken another step in his budding football career, captaining the Inter Miami Academy to the Naples Cup title and giving fans another glimpse of the youngster's footballing journey.Mateo, Messi's second son, was part of the Inter Miami Academy side that emerged victorious at the Copa Naples, with the achievement drawing attention across social media. The youngster was seen celebrating with the trophy after the triumph, proudly posing for photographs with the Copa Naples Cup, which carried the word 'champion'.Inter Miami's academy confirmed that its teams from the U-8 through U-12 age groups were competing in the 2026 Copa Naples, held at the Paradise Coast Sports Complex in Naples, Florida, on September 5 and 6.The title represents another memorable moment in Mateo's early football journey as he continues to develop within Inter Miami's youth setup.Mateo follows in Messi's footstepsMateo is the second of Lionel Messi and Antonela Roccuzzo's three sons. He will turn 11 on September 11, with his older brother Thiago 13 and younger brother Ciro eight.While his father has already established himself as one of the greatest players in football history, Mateo has gradually attracted attention for his own footballing ability.Videos of Mateo playing football have previously gone viral, with his skills, goals and competitive nature drawing comparisons with his famous father. His latest achievement, however, came not through a social-media clip but on the youth football circuit, where he helped lead Inter Miami Academy to a tournament title.Social media users were quick to celebrate the achievement after images of Mateo with the trophy circulated online. A video shared by Spanish publication Marca showed the youngster smiling for the cameras while holding the Copa Naples trophy.The Naples Cup triumph comes at an interesting time for the Messi family, with Lionel Messi himself having recently closed one major chapter of his career.A new chapter for the Messi familyMessi recently announced his retirement from international football after a remarkable 21-year career with Argentina. The decision came after Argentina's defeat to Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final, where Messi's side finished runners-up. Messi had said the decision was painful but necessary after he had given everything to the national side.The 39-year-old had previously fulfilled his biggest international ambition by leading Argentina to the 2022 World Cup title in Qatar.His international career may now be over, but Messi remains active at club level with Inter Miami. He recently assisted Casemiro's goal in a 2-2 draw against Atlanta United in his first club appearance after announcing his international retirement.That makes Mateo's Naples Cup success another intriguing development in a football family whose connection with the sport continues across generations.For now, Mateo remains at the beginning of his journey. But by captaining an Inter Miami Academy side to a tournament title and lifting the Naples Cup trophy, the youngster has added another notable achievement to a football story that is only just beginning.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Getafe - Celta de Vigo: horario, dónde ver en TV y canal del partido de LaLiga EA Sports
articles.standfirst: Getafe y Celta de Vigo se enfrentan hoy en el Estadio Coliseum en el partido correspondiente a la jornada 4 de LaLiga EA Sports.
articles.summary: Getafe y Celta de Vigo se enfrentan hoy en el Estadio Coliseum en el partido correspondiente a la jornada 4 de LaLiga EA Sports.
articles.body: El Getafe arranca un periplo de cuatro partidos en apenas trece días en el que los azulones buscarán escalar posiciones en la tabla y amarrar un buen puñado de puntos de cara al objetivo de la permanencia marcada por el conjunto azulón después de un mal inicio. Tampoco ha empezado mejor el Celta, otro de nuestros representantes en competición europea, que necesita sumar puntos antes de que empiece la Europa League para no meterse en un jaleo. El partido de Liga entre Getafe y Celta de Vigo se podrá ver por televisión en directo a través del canal Movistar LaLiga. También se podrá seguir el partido a través de la narración de Radio MARCA y con los comentarios en directo de MARCA.com. Desde dos horas antes, sigue la previa y los onces. Tras el encuentro, podrás leer la crónica, las declaraciones de los protagonistas y ver el resumen con las mejores jugadas y los goles. El partido entre Getafe y Celta de Vigo se juega hoy lunes 7 de septiembre a las 19:00 horas. El Getafe llega al partido contra el Celta tras perder contra Osasuna, ahora mismo se encuentran en la posición número 14 con 3 puntos. El Celta llega al partido contra el Getafe tras empatar contra la Real Sociedad, ahora mismo se encuentran en la posición número 16 con 2 puntos.

articles.title: WNBA Analyst Slams FIBA World Cup Officials Over Missed Foul On Caitlin Clark
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark went scoreless while refs missed calls in a near-disaster for Team USA.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark and officiating concerns go hand-in-hand. But things took a heavy turn when the same debate returned over the weekend in Berlin, when Team USA edged Italy 55-52 at the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup.

On September 6, 2026, Team USA's 31-game winning run in the FIBA Women's World Cup came dangerously close to ending. Before Sunday, the United States' closest game during its winning run was a 2010 victory over Australia, 83-75.

On Sunday, Italy led 50-49 with 3:21 left when the United States rallied in the fourth quarter, making Team USA's 55-52 escape the closest FIBA World Cup match for the Americans since their last loss in 2006.

The Sunday game did get physical eventually, with Clark struggling to find her flow. Sports Illustrated writer and WNBA analyst Robin Lundberg voiced his frustration with the bad officiating involving the Indiana Fever star guard by pointing to a specific play. In particular, Lundberg cited prior uncalled contact from Olbis Andre of Italy in the paint and a missed foul on Clark's arm on a late first-half drive to the basket as proof of subpar refereeing.

Speaking on his YouTube channel about the missed foul call on Clark during the Sunday game, Lundberg said, "There were some other questionable plays in the game, like Caitlin, you know, drove to the basket late at the end of the first half. This is a clear foul across the arm that wasn't called. It's the off arm there on that play. Wasn't called a foul. Didn't get to the free-throw line, obviously."

In the first quarter, there was another incident that heightened the suspense. With 2:03 left in the first quarter, play stopped while officials deliberated over a foul call involving Clark.

Clark approached to give her opinion, provoking a sideline reaction from Italy's head coach, Andrea Capobianco.

Later, Capobianco was seen yelling across the court, to which Clark responded, according to professional lip readers, "Stop complaining."

After falling behind 23-8, Italy shifted to a 2-3 zone halfway through the first quarter, and the outcome was instant. By halftime, they had trimmed the lead to 30-24 after going on a 16-7 run. In the third quarter, they maintained their momentum and briefly seized the lead.

Team USA was only able to shoot 29 percent from the field and 1-for-12 from three-point range because of Italy's defense. Furthermore, Team USA's 55-point total was its lowest World Cup score since defeating Australia 42-38 in 1967.

Nevertheless, Lundberg wasn't the only one who had concerns about the officiating. On X (formerly Twitter), sports commentator Jason Whitlock voiced a similar grievance.

Addressing the physicality of the Sunday game, Whitlock wrote, "That was a brutal game of basketball. If the refs are going to allow that level of physicality, there's a good chance we won't win."

Attributing Team USA's struggle to A'ja Wilson's absence and Italy's physicality, Whitlock added in the same post on X, "We missed A'ja Wilson today. The physicality eliminated CC and bothered (Breanna) Stewart throughout and slowed (Aliyah) Boston late. Ugly hoops."

Just days before the World Cup, Wilson was sidelined due to lingering back and health issues.

Although it's unlikely that they could play a worse game than that, Team USA has to improve overall and get more from Napheesa Collier, Breanna Stewart, and Clark.

Just like the final score, the individual stats for Team USA were equally rough. Clark had her first scoreless game from the field at any level of basketball, finishing 0-for-6 with one free throw. Before making her ninth shot, Stewart missed her first eight.

According to ESPN Insights , Stewart, Cooper, and Clark, who were all among the top seven scorers in the WNBA this season, shot 1-for-19 together with Kahleah Copper.

For the first time since the 2006 defeat to Russia, Team USA scored fewer than 70 points in a World Cup match on Sunday.
